newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's first futures market to open in July.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's first futures market to open in July.

text.p: Venezuela's first futures market will open in July after a first May opening date was postponed for technical reasons, the head of the Venezuelan Options and Futures Chamber (Cacofv) said.
Cacofv President Jose Gonzalo Muci told Reuters that phone lines to operate the system had now been installed and a linkup to the Caracas Stock Exchange finally completed.
"We'll be conducting the first tests on July 7 ... the market will definitely open in July," he said.
Cacofv was given the go-ahead to start a futures and options market by the Venezuelan Securities Commission (CNV) in March.
Trading is due to start with bolivar/dollar exchange rate futures. Interest rate and Caracas Stock Exchange index .IBC futures will follow.
Cacofv counts the country's largest banks among its shareholders including Banco Provincial, Mercantil and Union.
